en.headline: Li Ka-shing funds Asia-first non-invasive kidney tumour trials in Hong Kong
en.dek: The Li Ka Shing Foundation is funding 30 places at three private hospitals for histotripsy clinical trials treating kidney cancer without surgical incisions.
body: The Li Ka Shing Foundation announced on Wednesday that Hong Kong will host Asia’s first clinical trials of histotripsy for kidney tumours. The technology uses focused sound waves to break up tumours without cutting into the body.

CUHK Medical Centre, Gleneagles Hospital Hong Kong and Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital will each receive places under the funding for a total of 30 patients. The trials will examine the safety and effectiveness of the procedure for kidney cancer.

Histotripsy has already been used in Hong Kong for more than 400 patients over the past two years, mainly for liver tumours, and has also completed pancreatic tumour trials at two of the hospitals. The foundation previously donated machines to local medical centres and supported lower-cost treatment for eligible liver cancer patients.
The inventor of the technology, University of Michigan professor Zhen Xu, received a Golden Goose Award from the American Association for the Advancement of Science earlier this year for the work.

zh.headline: 李嘉誠資助組織碎化技術腎癌臨床試驗 香港成亞洲首個城市
zh.dek: 李嘉誠基金會向三間私家醫院提供合共30個名額，以組織碎化技術（Histotripsy）進行腎臟癌無創治療臨床試驗。
body: 李嘉誠基金會周三宣布，香港將成為亞洲首個進行組織碎化技術腎臟癌臨床試驗的城市。這項技術以聚焦超聲波擊碎腫瘤，無需開刀。
香港中文大學醫院、港怡醫院及養和醫院將獲資助合共30個名額。試驗將評估該程序治療腎臟癌的安全性及成效。
過去兩年，組織碎化技術已在香港為逾400名病人提供治療，主要針對肝腫瘤，並已在兩間醫院完成胰臟腫瘤臨床試驗。基金會早前亦向本地醫學中心捐贈儀器，並資助合資格肝癌病人以較低費用接受治療。
技術發明人、密歇根大學教授徐蓁今年較早時獲美國科學促進會頒發金鵝獎，表揚相關研究。
